title: Chapter 18: Art, Craft, Music & Dance of WB

items: Rabindra Sangeet — songs composed by Rabindranath Tagore; distinct genre; central to WB culture
Baul Music — mystical folk music of WB; UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (2008); Bauls are wandering minstrels
Bhawaiya — folk music of North Bengal (Cooch Behar, Jalpaiguri)
Jhumur — folk music of Purulia, Bankura, Bardhaman; tribal origin
Kirtan — devotional music; especially in Nadia and Nabadwip (Vaishnavism influence)
Rabindra Nritya — dance style developed by Tagore at Shantiniketan
Chhau — martial dance; Purulia (WB), Seraikela (Jharkhand), Mayurbhanj (Odisha); UNESCO heritage
Manipuri Dance — also performed in WB; one of 8 classical dances
Gambhira — folk dance and music from Malda region; Shiva worship

cells: Kolkata; scroll painting near Kalighat temple; 19th century; satirical themes
Medinipur area; story-telling through painted scrolls; "Patua" artists
Terracotta horse; icon of WB; from Panchmura village, Bankura
Bardhaman, Bankura; lost-wax casting; tribal craft; very ancient
Embroidered quilt; folk art; women's tradition across WB
Bishnupur; woven silk with mythological motifs; GI tag
Shankha; Kolkata craftsmen are famous; used in rituals
Purulia, Bankura, tribal areas; baskets, mats, furniture
